trigger: a sink throw launches the detached emit thread, stderr is a full pipe so the thread blocks inside fprintf(stderr) holding the stderr FILE lock, then the agent shuts down normally: teardown() completes (the worker is no longer wedged) and exit() blocks on that FILE lock
summary: This is a CODE defect (classified truth-contradiction because the schema has no defect value; the code comments and ledger also claimed the opposite). The first version of the fix wrote the diagnostic with fprintf/fflush on the detached thread. A thread blocked there holds the stderr FILE lock and a normal exit() (libstdc++ ios_base::Init dtor -> cerr.flush() -> fflush(stderr)) waits on it forever, with no watchdog armed once teardown() returned: a regression against the pre-fix bounded exit 5. Reproduced independently by compliance-officer, security-guardian, cpp-expert, cpp-safety, cross-platform, unhappy-path and sre (gdb traces), and by the orchestrator against the real code (fprintf: killed by timeout; raw write: rc=0 in 0.4 s, delivery 2/2). The ledger and code comments claimed the thread was 'safe to be running at process exit'. Fixed: default_stderr_emit formats into a stack buffer and issues one raw write(2) / WriteFile, holding no stdio lock; U12 (real write, blocked pipe, fflush prober) fails against fprintf. Windows/macOS exit paths reasoned, not run. This closes only the diagnostic-write half of 4666pr2-gov-stderr-wedge-still-open-worker-thread (governance.d/4666-pr2-hardening-gate8-round3.Kx7pRw.jsonl): the console-sink half of that wedge is 5023-gov-console-sink-wedge-untracked below and is NOT closed.

trigger: an agent whose sink list includes stderr or stdout (a stdout sink with no --log-file, the shipped systemd/Docker default; a stderr sink beside the file sink with --log-file outside a Windows service) with that fd on a stalled pipe
summary: The changelog headline, server-admin.md, the header banner and the handler comment said a blocked stderr can no longer stall log delivery. That is only true for the diagnostic's own write: a console sink on the same blocked fd still stalls the worker in that sink's own write (verified independently by enterprise-readiness, compliance-officer, docs-writer, security-guardian, cpp-safety, sre, cross-platform, unhappy-path and consistency-auditor). On POSIX the vendored spdlog console sink ignores a failed write, so a blocked console fd BLOCKS the worker rather than reaching the handler (on Windows a WriteFile failure does throw, but a blocked write has not failed), and a file sink implies a stderr sink outside a Windows service, so on shipped Linux/macOS configs the handler's stderr write matters mainly for producer-thread triggers and setups where stderr is not a sink. Severity derivation DISAGREED across reviewers: sre derived HIGH (I6 false assurance), cpp-safety and consistency-auditor LOW, the rest MEDIUM. Adjudicated conservatively as BLOCKING; the fix is the same either way. Fixed by scoping every claim (changelog, manual, hpp banner, cpp comment, ledger rows 20/21) to the diagnostic write and stating the console-sink residual, the shutdown-watchdog bound, and an operator troubleshooting path. Round 2 then corrected the residual sentence to say usable --log-file (5023-gov2-scope-omits-unopenable-log-file) and the changelog headline (5023-gov2-changelog-hang-claim).

summary: By design of the single-worker, serial-sink primitive a stuck sink stalls the worker (producers keep going, oldest lines drop). Not introduced or worsened by this change, bounded only at shutdown by teardown's watchdog, exposed by stalled_for() (an accessor only: nothing in agents/ or server/ reads it, so the stall is not production-observable). No existing issue tracks isolating sinks from each other; sre recommends one. Deliberately NOT filed by the orchestrator: it is a design-level decision for the maintainer. Now stated plainly in the changelog, manual, banner, comments and ledger. Round 2 (compliance-officer) noted that both commit messages carry Closes #5023, which would remove the only tracker of the worker-stall hazard; whether to file or park an issue for it, and whether the PR says Closes or Refs, is the maintainer call and is asked at PR time.
